buddy.title: Content Design AI Buddy
buddy.alt: Chat with the Content Design buddy recommending a designer reach out to Iara
buddy.summary: A hackathon proof of concept that became the design team’s daily content companion.
paras: During a hackathon, a fellow content designer and I created an AI-powered Content Design buddy to test a new way to support teams without dedicated content support.

After two months of testing and refining its instructions, it launched connected to our content strategy, guidelines, principles and word lists. It recognises design system components, so designers can prompt with text or images for microcopy ideas and strategy insights — and it tells them when to reach out to us.
Within a month it became the design team’s new best content friend, used daily by product designers and freeing our team for more strategic work.

order.title: Order tracking journey
order.alt: Mobile order details screen with packages and delivery progress
order.summary: End-to-end collaboration from discovery research to delivery.
paras: End-to-end collaboration with the product designer, UX researcher and product team, starting with discovery research, through collaborative solution design and delivery.
The project included a content-led usability test focused on understanding which content hierarchy would work best on the order details page.
order.caption: This is an AI-generated design concept for illustration purposes.

cancel.title: Cancellation flow
cancel.alt: Cancellation confirmation dialog inviting users to a research conversation
cancel.summary: Retention through transparency — a respectful, low-friction path.
paras: As the Senior Growth Content Designer, I refined the copy and information hierarchy across the entire cancellation flow.
The approach was rooted in transparency: clearly outlining the consequences of cancelling while avoiding guilt-tripping language.
We also created a research touchpoint — thanking users for working together, and inviting them to share their experience so we could learn from it.

wallet.title: Wallet & rewards at Booking.com
wallet.alt: Booking.com My Wallet and My Rewards screens
wallet.summary: Making a complex loyalty product feel easy to understand and trustworthy.
paras: As the UX Writer, I wrote the customer-facing copy for one of the first versions of Booking.com’s new travel rewards and wallet system, launching across devices and platforms.
Working with product teams in the FinTech unit, I kept language consistent across touchpoints and clearly explained how points, refunds and redemptions work.

Clarity over cleverness: short sentences, plain language and the most important information first — shaped by user testing and A/B results, in close collaboration with design, product and engineering.

agile.title: Agile planning tool beta launch
agile.alt: Epics beta planning board, settings and in-product banners
agile.summary: Leading UX writing for a brand-new product launch.
paras: I led the UX writing for the launch of a new agile planning tool: core UI copy, in-product promotional banners to drive feature awareness and adoption, and beta release notes for early users.
I collaborated closely with product teams and technical writers to keep messaging consistent across the product and its documentation, aligning content strategy with discovery and ongoing engagement.

bugaboo.title: Website replatforming at Bugaboo
bugaboo.alt: Collage of Bugaboo web pages, shopping cart and order emails
bugaboo.summary: Six months, one writer, an entire digital ecosystem.
paras: As the sole writer on the digital team, I led the creation of all digital content during a six-month overhaul of the entire digital ecosystem and website replatforming.
My role spanned UX writing, product content, SEO optimisation and brand content — creating new content for strategic highlights and refining existing content for the new launch.
Learnings: sharper project management, and proof of the power of collaborative, end-to-end content design.

library.title: Scaled content design library
library.alt: Searchable microcopy library inside the design tool
library.summary: A self-service library so product teams can write great UI copy on their own.
paras: A strategic initiative to decentralise content design support: a searchable library embedded in the design system, so product designers could prepare designs for critiques and showcases independently.
I led its creation in the content design team. It moved us away from repetitive microcopy polishing and reclaimed time for high-priority, strategic content work.

l10n.title: Translations workflow automation
l10n.alt: Before and after diagram of the translation workflow
l10n.summary: Bridging engineering and localization over an 8-month project.
paras: Acting as the bridge between engineering and localization, I defined requirements for a centralised, automated translation workflow and managed the feedback loop with translators and stakeholders.
I translated complex system logic into documentation and led cross-functional “Ask Me Anything” sessions for Product, Localization and Marketing.
It ensured the microcopy created and validated in research actually reached users in every language.

buddy.meta_title: Content Design AI Buddy · Project details · Iara Lucena
buddy.title: Content Design AI Buddy
buddy.lead: From a hackathon idea to a tool for every product designer.
buddy.img_alt: Chat with the Content Design buddy recommending a designer reach out to Iara
buddy.ov_p1: A generative AI content design buddy that a fellow content designer and I built, starting at a hackathon, and rolled out to all product designers.
buddy.ov_p2: It’s grounded in our content strategy, guidelines, principles and word lists, and it recognises design system components. Designers can prompt it with text or images to get microcopy ideas with the reasoning behind them, and it tells them when it’s time to involve a content designer.
buddy.pr_title: Demand for content design kept growing
buddy.pr_intro: The same gap looked different from each side of the table.
buddy.pr_a: Small microcopy requests competed with strategic work, and we saw a chance to connect our guidelines and the design system.
buddy.pr_b: Many product designers worked without a dedicated content designer and wanted to write good copy on their own.
buddy.hmw: How might we scale content design, without people bypassing it where it matters?
buddy.s1: Two content designers prototyped the buddy, with instructions connected to our guidelines and the design system.
buddy.s2: A demo for product design leadership to collect feedback: what was working well, and what to adjust to fit the design team’s needs.
buddy.s3: A pilot with a select group of designers. We collected their feedback and made small improvements.
buddy.s4: The proof of concept was made available to all product designers.
buddy.rs_title: What we set up, and what we learned
setup: Built for content designers and product designers
Covers the top 10 day-to-day use cases
Guidance on when to loop in and get help from a content designer when needed
Grounded in our guidelines, with the reasoning behind each suggestion
out: Designed to free content designers from routine microcopy
Aimed at helping designers without dedicated support move faster
learn: Teams work independently from first sketches to pre-launch; content design keeps final approval
AI amplifies your guidelines, so sharpen the craft first
Design the hand-off, not just the answers
Stage it: demo, pilot, adjust, scale
buddy.note: The escalation rules were key: the buddy was designed to extend content design, not replace it.
